scenes.visual: Show the title: Experiments That Distinguish Mechanisms. Introduce a depleted cell beside a rescued cell.

scenes.tts: Removing a protein can cause a defect. But that alone does not show that losing this protein caused it. The treatment may affect something else. Use independent controls, then put the protein back. If the defect goes away, rescue is strong evidence that losing the intended protein caused it. This matters because finding a protein in the right place at the right time does not show that it causes anything. These experiments test different questions.

scenes.visual: Show protein depletion followed by a defect, with two possible explanations: intended protein loss or an off-target effect. Add an independent control and a rescue branch. On rescue, restore the protein and normal behavior. Label the inference strong evidence, not certainty.

scenes.tts: A short hairpin R N A can reduce a protein by targeting its messenger R N A. Use another hairpin against a different region, and check that the protein is lost. For rescue, silent mutations change the messenger but keep the protein the same. The hairpin cannot pair with this version. Check that the rescue protein is made at about its normal level.
scenes.narration: A short hairpin RNA can reduce a protein by targeting its messenger RNA. Use another hairpin against a different region, and check that the protein is lost. scenes.visual: Compare hairpins targeting different regions of the same mRNA. Show an immunoblot checking depletion. Align original and rescue mRNAs; silent changes preserve the protein but prevent hairpin pairing. Compare rescue with an empty-vector control and show a normal-level expression check.

scenes.tts: Now ask which job matters. Depleting clathrin prolonged mitosis. Was that a spindle defect, or an indirect effect of losing endocytosis? Full-length resistant clathrin rescued mitosis. A shortened version partly rescued mitosis while failing to support transferrin uptake, the readout of endocytosis. Keeping part of one function while losing the other argues that the jobs are separate. Score both functions, rather than deciding from location alone.

scenes.visual: Show competing explanations for prolonged mitosis: spindle role or indirect loss of endocytosis. Compare depleted cells, full-length resistant rescue, and shortened resistant rescue. Display mitosis and transferrin-uptake readouts together. Show partial mitotic rescue for the shortened construct, never full recovery. Label this separation of function.

scenes.tts: A different question needs different evidence. In what order does secretory protein visit compartments? A short pulse of radioactive amino acid labels one batch. A chase with unlabelled amino acid lets you follow it. In pancreatic slices, label appeared first in E R fragments, then in Golgi fractions, then in the granule fraction. That gives an order. It does not choose between vesicles budding and fusing, and compartments maturing into one another.

scenes.visual: Track one labelled cohort through ER, Golgi, and the granule fraction in pancreatic slices. Distinguish fraction measurements from direct organelle identification; early granule-fraction label can be in condensing vacuoles. Under the same measured sequence, show budding/fusion and compartment maturation as alternative mechanisms, neither selected by timing alone.

scenes.tts: Finally, where does an enzyme live? In the lesson's made-up fractionation table, enzyme X follows the whole acid phosphatase profile, rather than the mitochondrial marker. That makes X provisionally lysosomal. Enrichment is not purity: fractions contain mixtures. Activity revealed by opening a membrane supports enclosure. A second lysosomal marker on a density gradient, and imaging in intact cells, would help confirm the assignment.

scenes.visual: Retain the whole-distribution comparison across N, M, L, P, S using the lesson's invented table. X follows acid phosphatase approximately; do not draw identical profiles. Contrast with cytochrome oxidase. Show mixed contents in the enriched fraction, then membrane opening revealing enzyme activity. End with a provisional lysosomal tag and checks using a second lysosomal marker on a density gradient and intact-cell imaging.
End card: Rescue tests causal attribution. Pulse-chase tests order. Fractionation tests compartment assignment.
